clue.text: Speak fast

definitions.meaning: to put a thought into words, to voice it
high-speed, as a non-stop train or delivery service

explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both senses: to state an opinion, and a rapid train or courier service.

clue.text: Works out manoeuvres

definitions.meaning: trains physically, as in a gym

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means does physical training; as a noun, troops' practice drills.

clue.text: Quiet region of Spain that's absolute perfection

parts.note: p is piano, softly, in music
Aragon is a region in north-east Spain

explanation.surface: A peaceful Spanish area is flawless.
explanation.definitionFit: A model of excellence, someone or something faultless.

clue.text: Made a change to get in lane such a bloomer!

indicators.note: altered, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A driver switched lanes, such a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a blunder, but here it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The eglantine is the sweet briar, a wild rose, so a flowering plant.

clue.text: Wine in a bag?

definitions.meaning: an old name for dry white wine from Spain, as Falstaff drank
a large coarse ... for carrying goods

explanation.surface: Wine sold in a bag, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: An old term for sherry-like fortified wine, and a large carrying pouch.

clue.text: Opposed to a donation for a gypsy

parts.note: V is short for versus, against, as in a fixture list
a grant is money given, a gift

explanation.surface: Someone objects to handing money to a traveller.
explanation.definitionFit: A wanderer with no settled home, the sense in which a roving traveller was once described.

clue.text: A bull never can be really defenceless

indicators.note: the letters can be turned into something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bull can never be truly helpless.
explanation.definitionFit: Open to attack or harm, exposed and unprotected.

clue.text: Huge gun protecting soldiers

indicators.note: the gun's letters go round the soldiers, shielding them

parts.note: gat is slang for a pistol
RE is the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: A massive weapon guarding troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Very big, immense in size.

clue.text: Before noon put up an aerial

parts.note: ante is Latin for before

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised upward means read from the bottom

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone installs a TV mast in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: A wire or rod that receives radio or television signals.

clue.text: An article about a note's number

indicators.note: the article's letters go round the note

parts.note: the is the definite article
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A piece of writing on a musical note's count.
explanation.definitionFit: A digit, the integer after two.

clue.text: Record made by eccentric loner

indicators.note: odd or off-centre, so the letters of the following word are rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd recluse has set down a register entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To put a name on an official list, as when signing up for a course.

clue.text: Pass the reader an accumulator

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
a lector reads lessons in church or lectures at a university

explanation.surface: Hand a battery over to the person reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who gathers and amasses things, such as stamps or coins.

clue.text: Shutting up about growing old

parts.note: C stands for circa, about, before a date
ageing, here in the shorter spelling

explanation.surface: Someone falls silent on the subject of getting older.
explanation.definitionFit: Confining in a cell or pen, putting behind bars.

clue.text: Fine as it may be, it must come to a stop

definitions.text: Fine as it may be, it must come to a stop

parts.words: Fine as it may be, it must come to a stop
parts.note: a fine is a penalty a judge may impose, and a written line of grammar must end with a full stop

explanation.surface: However good something is, it has to end.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a court's punishment and a grammatical unit closed by a full stop.

clue.text: Do away with all crooks!

parts.note: crooks sound like criminals, but they are bends, and removing every bend makes a thing true and level

explanation.definitionFit: To make something no longer bent or twisted.

clue.text: An area with low rainfall is in a mess

indicators.note: a muddle, so the letters of the three words before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: A dry region is in a state of disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a mess' reads as one phrase, but 'in a' belongs to the fodder with 'is', and only 'mess' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sinai peninsula between Egypt and Israel is largely desert.

clue.text: A device of people on the make!

definitions.text: A device of people on the make!

parts.words: A device of people on the make!
parts.note: people on the make sound like schemers, but are those in business, traders, and their device is a logo or emblem

explanation.surface: A trick used by the unscrupulous.
explanation.definitionFit: A registered emblem or name that identifies a company's goods.

clue.text: A cracking treat for youngsters in spring

definitions.text: A cracking treat for youngsters in spring

parts.words: A cracking treat for youngsters in spring
parts.note: cracking sounds like praise but is literal: a chocolate gift children break open at a spring festival

explanation.definitionFit: A chocolate ovoid given to children at the Christian festival in March or April.

clue.text: "Science is organised ———", wrote Spencer

parts.note: a quotation with its last word blanked out, from the Victorian philosopher Herbert Spencer

explanation.definitionFit: Herbert Spencer defined science as organised learning, the missing word completing his saying.

clue.text: Filibuster, so all went out of order

indicators.note: disarranged, so the letters of the three words are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A parliamentary delaying speech meant everything went awry.
explanation.definitionFit: To obstruct proceedings by delaying tactics, a political sense of blocking.

clue.text: Their sporting activity will involve them in a row

definitions.text: Their sporting activity will involve them in a row

parts.words: Their sporting activity will involve them in a row
parts.note: a row sounds like a quarrel, but it is pulling a boat with oars

explanation.definitionFit: Rowers of a racing boat propel it with blades.

clue.text: Make a start, though it's a struggle

definitions.meaning: a fight or scrap, a brief contest

explanation.surface: Getting going, even though it is hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb phrase it means get busy; hyphenated as a noun it means a bout of fighting.

clue.text: Woman at that point takes up Anglo-Saxon

parts.note: there means in that place

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters are read from the bottom

explanation.surface: A woman then adopts Old English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' is a link; only 'up' signals that the abbreviation is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, as of Mother Teresa or the politician May.

clue.text: Cereal cooked in the can

definitions.meaning: oats boiled in milk or water
slang for prison; British slang calls a jail term doing time this way

explanation.surface: Breakfast oats prepared from a tin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the can' is US and British slang for prison; in Britain doing porridge means serving a jail sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Boiled oatmeal, and British slang for time served behind bars.

clue.text: Walker, can get one into public relations

indicators.note: the word for one goes inside the abbreviation

parts.note: an ace is the one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A hiker can land a job in publicity.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse or person setting a walking or trotting rhythm, a strider.

clue.text: Princess with house in America

parts.note: Princess Ida is the Gilbert and Sullivan opera heroine

explanation.surface: A royal lady owns a home in the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: A north-western state of the USA, a place found in America.

clue.text: Let on about the meat

parts.note: re means concerning, as in a letter heading
veal is calf meat

explanation.surface: Someone gossips about what the butcher sells.
explanation.definitionFit: To disclose a secret, letting something be known.

clue.text: The limit for example of French ascendance

indicators.note: rising, so in a down entry the pieces are read from the bottom up

parts.note: eg is the abbreviation for exempli gratia
de is French for of

explanation.surface: The highest point reached by French power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ascendance' turns EGDE round, read upward in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A border or brink, the boundary of something.

clue.text: Firm politician did something — when pressed!

parts.note: CO is short for company, a business
MP is a Member of Parliament
acted means took action

explanation.surface: A company's MP only takes action when pushed.
explanation.definitionFit: Squeezed tightly together, made dense by force.

clue.text: In some ways little men do better

indicators.note: the answer sits partly within some of the clue's words

explanation.surface: Small men perform better in certain respects.
explanation.definitionFit: To correct or improve a text, a synonym of better as a verb.

clue.text: Review which is below par?

definitions.meaning: a summary or survey of points

explanation.definitionFit: Hyphenated it is a briefing that goes through items; as an adjective it means worn out.

clue.text: Cut in quarters with serious result

parts.note: E and N are compass points, two of the four quarters
grave means solemn

explanation.surface: Slicing something into four with grim consequences.
explanation.definitionFit: To carve letters or a design into a hard surface.
